Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
236 PM EDT Sun Sep 6 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 235 PM EDT Sunday...

No significant changes.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 235 PM EDT Sunday...

1. Dry and seasonable through Tuesday

2. A brief intrusion of tropical moisture on Thursday will give 
way to seasonable, dry conditions heading into the weekend

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 235 PM EDT Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: An upper low will remain centered just to the east 
heading into tomorrow, keeping the region in a seasonably cool 
airmass. Skies will continue to clear as it inches to the east and 
by tonight, the clouds should be mostly gone. This will set the 
stage for efficient radiational cooling, with lows generally falling 
into the 40s and upper 30s. The current forecast low at SLK is 37, 
but it could easily fall a few more degrees if winds go calm early. 
Warm air advection will begin for Monday and Tuesday, but it will be 
unsuccessful in causing a significant airmass change, with the 
humidity staying low and temperatures remaining around seasonable 
values. A few showers are possible in northern areas Monday night 
and early Tuesday morning as a dying cold front passes into the 
region.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A very humid air mass will quickly advect into Vermont 
and northern New York late Wednesday into early Thursday due to 
channeled flow stretching across the Great Lakes into New England 
with 100+ knot flow at 300mb. Flow will be fast down at 850mb as 
well, though the intensity of the LLJ has backed off towards 40-45 
knots. It will still result in a short duration of 2" PWATs across 
the region. Departing high pressure and the fast mid-level flow will 
result in fairly strong isentropic upglide. There should also be 
marginal CAPE of about 250 J/kg after dark on Wednesday for at least 
the St. Lawrence Valley (LREF ~40% > 250 J/kg, but expect that to 
percentage to increase as we get into the mesoscale model window). 
So moderate rain, perhaps briefly heavy, will race eastwards. Again, 
synoptic models are likely broad brushing rainfall amounts too much 
given the LLJ will produce west slope orographic enhancement and 
east slope terrain shadowing. The residence time of this moisture 
will be very short (5-9 hours) due to the fast flow, which will 
prevent significant rainfall totals. Broadly speaking, totals appear 
to range about 0.25-0.75", and we'll get towards the end of 
mesoscale models tomorrow for some of those finer details.

On Thursday, the tropical air mass will be gone, but there's still 
going to be a little moisture lingering. Marginal diurnally driven 
instability could produce a few showers Thursday afternoon, but 
it'll be generally warm in the 70s to near 80 while we await a cold 
front that'll pass through late Thursday night or Friday morning. 
Medium range guidance has shifted towards drier solutions for 
Friday. So we'll spend most all our weekend without rain as broad 
high pressure builds across the area. Some rain showers could begin 
approaching towards next Sunday evening when broad surface higher 
pressure will begin shifting offshore.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z SUNDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Through 18Z Monday...Stubborn stratocumulus clouds around 1000-2500
ft agl are finally dissipating, or lifting above 3000 ft, as dry air
and high pressure gradually build across the area. A spot shower or
two is possible, mainly over eastern Vermont through about 23z, but
the probabilities are low enough that there's no mention at any
terminal. North winds are 5-10 knots with a few gusts around 15-18
knots. Skies are expected to trend clear after sunset with surface
winds become light and variable. There will be some 10-15 knot flow
around 500 ft agl overnight, but sheltered river valleys and
elevated terrain basins will still likely produce fog. Noted some
IFR visibilities from 06z- 12z at KSLK and to a lesser extent at
KMPV. After 12z, generally SKC with northwest winds around 6-11
knots sustained, and perhaps a few gusts 16-19 knots after 15z.

Outlook...

Monday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Wednesday Night: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. Chance SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Thursday: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Thursday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Slight
chance SHRA.
Friday: VFR. NO SIG WX.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
